name: What is the typical process for trim replacement from start to finish?

mainEntity.name: What is the typical process for trim replacement from start to finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: The trim replacement process typically begins with an initial assessment and measurement of the areas needing work. Next, the old trim is carefully removed, ensuring no damage to the surrounding structure. Any damaged substrate or underlying wood is repaired or replaced. New trim pieces are then cut, fitted, and securely installed. Finally, the new trim is properly sealed, caulked, and prepared for painting or finishing. The process can vary based on the extent of damage and material chosen, affecting the overall timeline. Process clarity suggests discussing these steps with your contractor to set expectations.
acceptedAnswer.description: The process involves assessment, old trim removal, substrate repair, new trim installation, and finishing.
